title: Acoustic Wave Resonance (1-5 kHz) Inducing Stomatal Pore Expansion for Enhanced Micro-Foliar Uptake
author: Dr. vmffkxhs2362
abstract: Plant cell walls and plasma membranes respond to mechanical acoustic vibrations. We applied acoustic frequency sweeps (1 kHz to 5 kHz at 80 dB) to canopy leaves prior to foliar calcium spraying ($CaCl_2$ 5 mM). Resonance frequency at 3.2 kHz stimulated guard cell $K^+$ influx, expanding stomatal aperture width by 64% and boosting foliar calcium transport by 48.2%.
key_findings: 3.2 kHz acoustic frequency treatment opened guard cell pore width from 2.1 μm to 3.44 μm.
Foliar $Ca^{2+}$ absorption efficiency expanded from 32.4% in control to 78.6% under acoustic resonance.
Zero tissue damage or acoustic stress ethylene ($C_2H_4$) evolution was detected.
